One final-final mechanics tweak that actually makes everything cleaner and simpler to code (no weird half-expiring tickets).
New rule (replaces the previous ticket lifespan description):
→ Every time someone mints with a referral code, the referrer instantly gets two separate tickets added to their NFT:
+1 Small Block Ticket
+1 Big Block Ticket

Small Block ($2,500 pool → 5 × $500 draw):
Draw only from Small Block Tickets issued since the last small block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Small Block Tickets to 0.
Big Block ($100,000 pool → 5 × $20,000 draw):
Draw only from Big Block Tickets issued since the last big block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Big Block Tickets to 0.

Small blocks stay super fair and fresh (no one carries old tickets forward).
Big blocks naturally accumulate (people can see their big block entries climbing over weeks/months).

I see one issue. Coinbase Commerce is NOT a true fiat/credit card payment processor - it's a cryptocurrency payment gateway. Users still need crypto to pay!

Let me explain what's happening and provide real solutions:
Coinbase Commerce requires users to:
1\. Have cryptocurrency (USDC, ETH, BTC, etc.)
2\. Send it from their wallet to complete payment
3\. It's NOT accepting credit cards directly
This means it's not suitable for true non-crypto users who don't have any cryptocurrency.

Real Fiat On-Ramp Solutions
For TRUE credit card payments (Visa/Mastercard), you need different services:

Option 1: Stripe + Crypto (Recommended)
Best for: Direct card payments + automatic blockchain transactions
Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Users never need crypto
\- Lower fees than crypto payments
\- Familiar checkout experience

Cons:
\- Requires Stripe account verification
\- 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Option 2: Coinbase Pay (Different from Commerce)
Coinbase Pay (not Commerce) supports:
\- Credit card payments
\- OAuth authentication
\- Fiat → crypto conversion

Pros:
\- Uses the Coinbase brand trust
\- Integrated fiat → crypto

Cons:
\- Requires a Coinbase account
\- User needs to buy crypto first

Option 3: Third-Party Fiat Gateways
Services that do true fiat → crypto:
\- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget
\- Ramp Network - Fiat on-ramp widget
\- Wyre - Fiat gateway (being sunset)
\- Transak - Global fiat on-ramp

Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Pre-built widgets
\- Global coverage

Cons:
\- Higher fees (3-5%)
\- KYC requirements
\- User still sees crypto conversion

Yes — it’s doable, and it’s not “crazy complicated”, but it does require changing the on-chain flow (i.e., a contract update / redeploy of the NFT contract’s mintWithETH logic). Why it requires a contract change
Right now mintWithETH:
\- Wraps all msg.value into WETH
\- Swaps all WETH to USDC
\- If usdcReceived > 15 USDC, it refunds the difference in USDC

To refund ETH instead, the contract must not swap the full amount.

history.speaker: freelancer
history.text:
Best-practice approach (clean + safe UX)
Update mintWithETH to use Uniswap V3 exactOutputSingle:
\- Target exactly 15\_000\_000 USDC out
\- Provide amountInMaximum = msg.value WETH
\- Router uses only what’s needed
\- Contract unwraps leftover WETH and refunds ETH to the payer
\- Reverts if it can’t get 15 USDC within msg.value
\- This is the standard way to guarantee the exact USDC mint price and refund the remainder in ETH.

Recommendation
\- If you want zero surprises for users: implement exactOutputSingle + ETH refund (requires a redeploy).
\- If you want to keep things stable now: keep current behavior but add a short UI note like: “Excess is refunded in USDC.” (lowest risk).

Hey Joseph,
One final-final mechanics tweak that actually makes everything cleaner and simpler to code (no weird half-expiring tickets).
New rule (replaces the previous ticket lifespan description):
→ Every time someone mints with a referral code, the referrer instantly gets two separate tickets added to their NFT:
+1 Small Block Ticket
+1 Big Block Ticket

These are two completely independent counters.
Small Block ($2,500 pool → 5 × $500 draw):
Draw only from Small Block Tickets issued since the last small block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Small Block Tickets to 0.
Big Block ($100,000 pool → 5 × $20,000 draw):
Draw only from Big Block Tickets issued since the last big block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Big Block Tickets to 0.

This way:
Small blocks stay super fair and fresh (no one carries old tickets forward).
Big blocks naturally accumulate (people can see their big block entries climbing over weeks/months).
Metadata is trivial: just show the two counters + permanent badges.

Triggers stay pool-based (small block fires the moment small pool = exactly $2,500, big block when big pool = exactly $100,000). Secondary royalties still fill pools but don’t create tickets.
Everything else stays identical (auto $5 commission, random ticket to existing NFT when no ref used, manual claim, etc.).
This version should be easier to implement and explain to users.
Sorry for the flip-flop — Once you confirm this is cleaner for you too, we’re 100% locked.

Thanks man!

I see one issue. Coinbase Commerce is NOT a true fiat/credit card payment processor - it's a cryptocurrency payment gateway. Users still need crypto to pay!

Let me explain what's happening and provide real solutions:
Coinbase Commerce requires users to:
1\. Have cryptocurrency (USDC, ETH, BTC, etc.)
2\. Send it from their wallet to complete payment
3\. It's NOT accepting credit cards directly
This means it's not suitable for true non-crypto users who don't have any cryptocurrency.

Real Fiat On-Ramp Solutions
For TRUE credit card payments (Visa/Mastercard), you need different services:

Option 1: Stripe + Crypto (Recommended)
Best for: Direct card payments + automatic blockchain transactions
Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Users never need crypto
\- Lower fees than crypto payments
\- Familiar checkout experience

Cons:
\- Requires Stripe account verification
\- 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Option 2: Coinbase Pay (Different from Commerce)
Coinbase Pay (not Commerce) supports:
\- Credit card payments
\- OAuth authentication
\- Fiat → crypto conversion

Pros:
\- Uses the Coinbase brand trust
\- Integrated fiat → crypto

Cons:
\- Requires a Coinbase account
\- User needs to buy crypto first

Option 3: Third-Party Fiat Gateways
Services that do true fiat → crypto:
\- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget
\- Ramp Network - Fiat on-ramp widget
\- Wyre - Fiat gateway (being sunset)
\- Transak - Global fiat on-ramp

Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Pre-built widgets
\- Global coverage

Cons:
\- Higher fees (3-5%)
\- KYC requirements
\- User still sees crypto conversion

I see one issue. Coinbase Commerce is NOT a true fiat/credit card payment processor - it's a cryptocurrency payment gateway. Users still need crypto to pay!

Let me explain what's happening and provide real solutions:
Coinbase Commerce requires users to:
1\. Have cryptocurrency (USDC, ETH, BTC, etc.)
2\. Send it from their wallet to complete payment
3\. It's NOT accepting credit cards directly
This means it's not suitable for true non-crypto users who don't have any cryptocurrency.

Real Fiat On-Ramp Solutions
For TRUE credit card payments (Visa/Mastercard), you need different services:

Option 1: Stripe + Crypto (Recommended)
Best for: Direct card payments + automatic blockchain transactions
Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Users never need crypto
\- Lower fees than crypto payments
\- Familiar checkout experience

Cons:
\- Requires Stripe account verification
\- 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Option 2: Coinbase Pay (Different from Commerce)
Coinbase Pay (not Commerce) supports:
\- Credit card payments
\- OAuth authentication
\- Fiat → crypto conversion

Pros:
\- Uses the Coinbase brand trust
\- Integrated fiat → crypto

Cons:
\- Requires a Coinbase account
\- User needs to buy crypto first

Option 3: Third-Party Fiat Gateways
Services that do true fiat → crypto:
\- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget
\- Ramp Network - Fiat on-ramp widget
\- Wyre - Fiat gateway (being sunset)
\- Transak - Global fiat on-ramp

Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Pre-built widgets
\- Global coverage

Cons:
\- Higher fees (3-5%)
\- KYC requirements
\- User still sees crypto conversion

Yes — it’s doable, and it’s not “crazy complicated”, but it does require changing the on-chain flow (i.e., a contract update / redeploy of the NFT contract’s mintWithETH logic). With the current design (swap full msg.value → USDC, then refund excess in USDC), the contract simply doesn’t have a path to refund ETH.

Why it requires a contract change
Right now mintWithETH:
\- Wraps all msg.value into WETH
\- Swaps all WETH to USDC
\- If usdcReceived > 15 USDC, it refunds the difference in USDC

To refund ETH instead, the contract must not swap the full amount.

history.speaker: freelancer
history.text:
Best-practice approach (clean + safe UX)
Update mintWithETH to use Uniswap V3 exactOutputSingle:
\- Target exactly 15\_000\_000 USDC out
\- Provide amountInMaximum = msg.value WETH
\- Router uses only what’s needed
\- Contract unwraps leftover WETH and refunds ETH to the payer
\- Reverts if it can’t get 15 USDC within msg.value
\- This is the standard way to guarantee the exact USDC mint price and refund the remainder in ETH.

Recommendation
\- If you want zero surprises for users: implement exactOutputSingle + ETH refund (requires a redeploy).
\- If you want to keep things stable now: keep current behavior but add a short UI note like: “Excess is refunded in USDC.” (lowest risk).

Hey Joseph,
One final-final mechanics tweak that actually makes everything cleaner and simpler to code (no weird half-expiring tickets).
New rule (replaces the previous ticket lifespan description):
→ Every time someone mints with a referral code, the referrer instantly gets two separate tickets added to their NFT:
+1 Small Block Ticket
+1 Big Block Ticket

These are two completely independent counters.
Small Block ($2,500 pool → 5 × $500 draw):
Draw only from Small Block Tickets issued since the last small block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Small Block Tickets to 0.
Big Block ($100,000 pool → 5 × $20,000 draw):
Draw only from Big Block Tickets issued since the last big block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Big Block Tickets to 0.

This way:
Small blocks stay super fair and fresh (no one carries old tickets forward).
Big blocks naturally accumulate (people can see their big block entries climbing over weeks/months).
Metadata is trivial: just show the two counters + permanent badges.

Triggers stay pool-based (small block fires the moment small pool = exactly $2,500, big block when big pool = exactly $100,000). Secondary royalties still fill pools but don’t create tickets.
Everything else stays identical (auto $5 commission, random ticket to existing NFT when no ref used, manual claim, etc.).
This version should be easier to implement and explain to users.

I see one issue. Coinbase Commerce is NOT a true fiat/credit card payment processor - it's a cryptocurrency payment gateway. Users still need crypto to pay!

Let me explain what's happening and provide real solutions:
Coinbase Commerce requires users to:
1\. Have cryptocurrency (USDC, ETH, BTC, etc.)
2\. Send it from their wallet to complete payment
3\. It's NOT accepting credit cards directly
This means it's not suitable for true non-crypto users who don't have any cryptocurrency.

Real Fiat On-Ramp Solutions
For TRUE credit card payments (Visa/Mastercard), you need different services:

Option 1: Stripe + Crypto (Recommended)
Best for: Direct card payments + automatic blockchain transactions
Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Users never need crypto
\- Lower fees than crypto payments
\- Familiar checkout experience

Cons:
\- Requires Stripe account verification
\- 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Option 2: Coinbase Pay (Different from Commerce)
Coinbase Pay (not Commerce) supports:
\- Credit card payments
\- OAuth authentication
\- Fiat → crypto conversion

Pros:
\- Uses the Coinbase brand trust
\- Integrated fiat → crypto

Cons:
\- Requires a Coinbase account
\- User needs to buy crypto first

Option 3: Third-Party Fiat Gateways
Services that do true fiat → crypto:
\- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget
\- Ramp Network - Fiat on-ramp widget
\- Wyre - Fiat gateway (being sunset)
\- Transak - Global fiat on-ramp

Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Pre-built widgets
\- Global coverage

Cons:
\- Higher fees (3-5%)
\- KYC requirements
\- User still sees crypto conversion

Yes — it’s doable, and it’s not “crazy complicated”, but it does require changing the on-chain flow (i.e., a contract update / redeploy of the NFT contract’s mintWithETH logic). With the current design (swap full msg.value → USDC, then refund excess in USDC), the contract simply doesn’t have a path to refund ETH.

Why it requires a contract change
Right now mintWithETH:
\- Wraps all msg.value into WETH
\- Swaps all WETH to USDC
\- If usdcReceived > 15 USDC, it refunds the difference in USDC

To refund ETH instead, the contract must not swap the full amount.

history.speaker: freelancer
history.text:
Best-practice approach (clean + safe UX)
Update mintWithETH to use Uniswap V3 exactOutputSingle:
\- Target exactly 15\_000\_000 USDC out
\- Provide amountInMaximum = msg.value WETH
\- Router uses only what’s needed
\- Contract unwraps leftover WETH and refunds ETH to the payer
\- Reverts if it can’t get 15 USDC within msg.value
\- This is the standard way to guarantee the exact USDC mint price and refund the remainder in ETH.

Recommendation
\- If you want zero surprises for users: implement exactOutputSingle + ETH refund (requires a redeploy).
\- If you want to keep things stable now: keep current behavior but add a short UI note like: “Excess is refunded in USDC.” (lowest risk).

Let me explain what's happening and provide real solutions:
Coinbase Commerce requires users to:
1\. Have cryptocurrency (USDC, ETH, BTC, etc.)
2\. Send it from their wallet to complete payment
3\. It's NOT accepting credit cards directly
This means it's not suitable for true non-crypto users who don't have any cryptocurrency.

Real Fiat On-Ramp Solutions
For TRUE credit card payments (Visa/Mastercard), you need different services:

Option 1: Stripe + Crypto (Recommended)
Best for: Direct card payments + automatic blockchain transactions
Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Users never need crypto
\- Lower fees than crypto payments
\- Familiar checkout experience

Cons:
\- Requires Stripe account verification
\- 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Option 2: Coinbase Pay (Different from Commerce)
Coinbase Pay (not Commerce) supports:
\- Credit card payments
\- OAuth authentication
\- Fiat → crypto conversion

Pros:
\- Uses the Coinbase brand trust
\- Integrated fiat → crypto

Cons:
\- Requires a Coinbase account
\- User needs to buy crypto first

Option 3: Third-Party Fiat Gateways
Services that do true fiat → crypto:
\- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget
\- Ramp Network - Fiat on-ramp widget
\- Wyre - Fiat gateway (being sunset)
\- Transak - Global fiat on-ramp

Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Pre-built widgets
\- Global coverage

Cons:
\- Higher fees (3-5%)
\- KYC requirements
\- User still sees crypto conversion

Purchase your ebook NFT for $15 USD. Your mint number is your referral code.

Earn Through Referrals
Share your mint number or link. Instantly earn $5 USD every time someone mints using it. No limits, no expiration.
If no code is used → $5 + tickets go to a random existing ticket holder.

Accumulate Tickets
Each referral also gives you Small & Big Block prize tickets for the current blocks.
More referrals = more tickets = better chances.

Win Prizes
Small Block: 5 × $500 every 500 sales.
Big Block: 5 × $10,000 every 50,000 sales.
(Sales = mint + secondary)
Winners selected randomly and fairly via Chainlink VRF.

Claim Your Rewards
Commissions sent automatically on-chain. Prizes announced on the Winners page — claim with one click whenever you're ready.

Key Features

Automatic Rewards: Smart contracts handle all payments instantly.
Fair Prize Selection: Chainlink VRF ensures true randomness.
Yield Generation: Prize pools earn yield through Aave integration.
Gamification: Badges and leaderboards make it fun and competitive.
Transparency: All transactions and rules on-chain and verifiable.
Low Fees: Built on Base for speed and minimal transaction costs.

Our Vision
Project Rebuild starts with one book, but this is only the beginning.
We envision a world where ebooks succeed on merit alone, free from the gatekeepers and Amazon algorithms drowning indie voices.
Where creators (unknown or established) rise because their work resonates, not because they game a platform, have the connections or buy enough ads.
Where fans get paid for the word-of-mouth marketing they've always done for free, and where any hustler can jump in to earn if they spot a gem worth spreading.

Our goal: a self-sustaining model that benefits everyone.
Artists earn their fair share, fans & affiliates build real income, communities forge direct bonds — transforming one underdog's recovery into a decentralized revolution for all creators.
All without hype, just aligned incentives.

One final-final mechanics tweak that actually makes everything cleaner and simpler to code (no weird half-expiring tickets).
New rule (replaces the previous ticket lifespan description):
→ Every time someone mints with a referral code, the referrer instantly gets two separate tickets added to their NFT:
+1 Small Block Ticket
+1 Big Block Ticket

Small Block ($2,500 pool → 5 × $500 draw):
Draw only from Small Block Tickets issued since the last small block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Small Block Tickets to 0.
Big Block ($100,000 pool → 5 × $20,000 draw):
Draw only from Big Block Tickets issued since the last big block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Big Block Tickets to 0.

This way:
Small blocks stay super fair and fresh (no one carries old tickets forward).
Big blocks naturally accumulate (people can see their big block entries climbing over weeks/months).
Metadata is trivial: just show the two counters + permanent badges.

Triggers stay pool-based (small block fires the moment small pool = exactly $2,500, big block when big pool = exactly $100,000). Secondary royalties still fill pools but don’t create tickets.
Everything else stays identical (auto $5 commission, random ticket to existing NFT when no ref used, manual claim, etc.).

I see one issue. Coinbase Commerce is NOT a true fiat/credit card payment processor - it's a cryptocurrency payment gateway. Users still need crypto to pay!

Let me explain what's happening and provide real solutions:
Coinbase Commerce requires users to:
1\. Have cryptocurrency (USDC, ETH, BTC, etc.)
2\. Send it from their wallet to complete payment
3\. It's NOT accepting credit cards directly
This means it's not suitable for true non-crypto users who don't have any cryptocurrency.

Real Fiat On-Ramp Solutions
For TRUE credit card payments (Visa/Mastercard), you need different services:

Option 1: Stripe + Crypto (Recommended)
Best for: Direct card payments + automatic blockchain transactions
Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Users never need crypto
\- Lower fees than crypto payments
\- Familiar checkout experience

Cons:
\- Requires Stripe account verification
\- 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Option 2: Coinbase Pay (Different from Commerce)
Coinbase Pay (not Commerce) supports:
\- Credit card payments
\- OAuth authentication
\- Fiat → crypto conversion

Pros:
\- Uses the Coinbase brand trust
\- Integrated fiat → crypto

Cons:
\- Requires a Coinbase account
\- User needs to buy crypto first

Option 3: Third-Party Fiat Gateways
Services that do true fiat → crypto:
\- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget
\- Ramp Network - Fiat on-ramp widget
\- Wyre - Fiat gateway (being sunset)
\- Transak - Global fiat on-ramp

Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Pre-built widgets
\- Global coverage

Cons:
\- Higher fees (3-5%)
\- KYC requirements
\- User still sees crypto conversion

Coinbase Commerce requires users to:
1\. Have cryptocurrency (USDC, ETH, BTC, etc.)
2\. Send it from their wallet to complete payment
3\. It's NOT accepting credit cards directly
This means it's not suitable for true non-crypto users who don't have any cryptocurrency.

Real Fiat On-Ramp Solutions
For TRUE credit card payments (Visa/Mastercard), you need different services:

Option 1: Stripe + Crypto (Recommended)
Best for: Direct card payments + automatic blockchain transactions
Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Users never need crypto
\- Lower fees than crypto payments
\- Familiar checkout experience

Cons:
\- Requires Stripe account verification
\- 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Option 2: Coinbase Pay (Different from Commerce)
Coinbase Pay (not Commerce) supports:
\- Credit card payments
\- OAuth authentication
\- Fiat → crypto conversion

Pros:
\- Uses the Coinbase brand trust
\- Integrated fiat → crypto

Cons:
\- Requires a Coinbase account
\- User needs to buy crypto first

Option 3: Third-Party Fiat Gateways
Services that do true fiat → crypto:
\- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget
\- Ramp Network - Fiat on-ramp widget
\- Wyre - Fiat gateway (being sunset)
\- Transak - Global fiat on-ramp

Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Pre-built widgets
\- Global coverage

Cons:
\- Higher fees (3-5%)
\- KYC requirements
\- User still sees crypto conversion

One final-final mechanics tweak that actually makes everything cleaner and simpler to code (no weird half-expiring tickets).
New rule (replaces the previous ticket lifespan description):
→ Every time someone mints with a referral code, the referrer instantly gets two separate tickets added to their NFT:
+1 Small Block Ticket

Small Block ($2,500 pool → 5 × $500 draw):
Draw only from Small Block Tickets issued since the last small block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Small Block Tickets to 0.
Big Block ($100,000 pool → 5 × $20,000 draw):

I see one issue. Coinbase Commerce is NOT a true fiat/credit card payment processor - it's a cryptocurrency payment gateway. Users still need crypto to pay!

Let me explain what's happening and provide real solutions:
Coinbase Commerce requires users to:
1\. Have cryptocurrency (USDC, ETH, BTC, etc.)
2\. Send it from their wallet to complete payment
3\. It's NOT accepting credit cards directly
This means it's not suitable for true non-crypto users who don't have any cryptocurrency.

Real Fiat On-Ramp Solutions
For TRUE credit card payments (Visa/Mastercard), you need different services:

Option 1: Stripe + Crypto (Recommended)
Best for: Direct card payments + automatic blockchain transactions
Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Users never need crypto
\- Lower fees than crypto payments
\- Familiar checkout experience

Cons:
\- Requires Stripe account verification
\- 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Option 2: Coinbase Pay (Different from Commerce)
Coinbase Pay (not Commerce) supports:
\- Credit card payments
\- OAuth authentication
\- Fiat → crypto conversion

Pros:
\- Uses the Coinbase brand trust
\- Integrated fiat → crypto

Cons:
\- Requires a Coinbase account
\- User needs to buy crypto first

Option 3: Third-Party Fiat Gateways
Services that do true fiat → crypto:
\- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget
\- Ramp Network - Fiat on-ramp widget
\- Wyre - Fiat gateway (being sunset)
\- Transak - Global fiat on-ramp

Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Pre-built widgets
\- Global coverage

Cons:
\- Higher fees (3-5%)
\- KYC requirements
\- User still sees crypto conversion

I see one issue. Coinbase Commerce is NOT a true fiat/credit card payment processor - it's a cryptocurrency payment gateway. Users still need crypto to pay!

Let me explain what's happening and provide real solutions:
Coinbase Commerce requires users to:
1\. Have cryptocurrency (USDC, ETH, BTC, etc.)
2\. Send it from their wallet to complete payment
3\. It's NOT accepting credit cards directly
This means it's not suitable for true non-crypto users who don't have any cryptocurrency.

Real Fiat On-Ramp Solutions
For TRUE credit card payments (Visa/Mastercard), you need different services:

Option 1: Stripe + Crypto (Recommended)
Best for: Direct card payments + automatic blockchain transactions
Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Users never need crypto
\- Lower fees than crypto payments
\- Familiar checkout experience

Cons:
\- Requires Stripe account verification
\- 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Option 2: Coinbase Pay (Different from Commerce)
Coinbase Pay (not Commerce) supports:
\- Credit card payments
\- OAuth authentication
\- Fiat → crypto conversion

Pros:
\- Uses the Coinbase brand trust
\- Integrated fiat → crypto

Cons:
\- Requires a Coinbase account
\- User needs to buy crypto first

Option 3: Third-Party Fiat Gateways
Services that do true fiat → crypto:
\- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget
\- Ramp Network - Fiat on-ramp widget
\- Wyre - Fiat gateway (being sunset)
\- Transak - Global fiat on-ramp

Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Pre-built widgets
\- Global coverage

Cons:
\- Higher fees (3-5%)
\- KYC requirements
\- User still sees crypto conversion

\- Target exactly 15\_000\_000 USDC out
\- Provide amountInMaximum = msg.value WETH
\- Router uses only what’s needed
\- Contract unwraps leftover WETH and refunds ETH to the payer
\- Reverts if it can’t get 15 USDC within msg.value
\- This is the standard way to guarantee the exact USDC mint price and refund the remainder in ETH.

\- If you want to keep things stable now: keep current behavior but add a short UI note like: “Excess is refunded in USDC.” (lowest risk).

Hey Joseph,
One final-final mechanics tweak that actually makes everything cleaner and simpler to code (no weird half-expiring tickets).
New rule (replaces the previous ticket lifespan description):
→ Every time someone mints with a referral code, the referrer instantly gets two separate tickets added to their NFT:
+1 Small Block Ticket
+1 Big Block Ticket

These are two completely independent counters.
Small Block ($2,500 pool → 5 × $500 draw):
Draw only from Small Block Tickets issued since the last small block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Small Block Tickets to 0.
Big Block ($100,000 pool → 5 × $20,000 draw):
Draw only from Big Block Tickets issued since the last big block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Big Block Tickets to 0.

This way:
Small blocks stay super fair and fresh (no one carries old tickets forward).

Big Block ($100,000 pool → 5 × $20,000 draw):

I see one issue. Coinbase Commerce is NOT a true fiat/credit card payment processor - it's a cryptocurrency payment gateway. Users still need crypto to pay!

Let me explain what's happening and provide real solutions:
Coinbase Commerce requires users to:
1\. Have cryptocurrency (USDC, ETH, BTC, etc.)
2\. Send it from their wallet to complete payment
3\. It's NOT accepting credit cards directly
This means it's not suitable for true non-crypto users who don't have any cryptocurrency.

Real Fiat On-Ramp Solutions
For TRUE credit card payments (Visa/Mastercard), you need different services:

Option 1: Stripe + Crypto (Recommended)
Best for: Direct card payments + automatic blockchain transactions
Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Users never need crypto
\- Lower fees than crypto payments
\- Familiar checkout experience

Cons:
\- Requires Stripe account verification
\- 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Option 2: Coinbase Pay (Different from Commerce)
Coinbase Pay (not Commerce) supports:
\- Credit card payments
\- OAuth authentication
\- Fiat → crypto conversion

Pros:
\- Uses the Coinbase brand trust
\- Integrated fiat → crypto

Cons:
\- Requires a Coinbase account
\- User needs to buy crypto first

Option 3: Third-Party Fiat Gateways
Services that do true fiat → crypto:
\- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget
\- Ramp Network - Fiat on-ramp widget
\- Wyre - Fiat gateway (being sunset)
\- Transak - Global fiat on-ramp

Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Pre-built widgets
\- Global coverage

Cons:
\- Higher fees (3-5%)
\- KYC requirements
\- User still sees crypto conversion

Big Block ($100,000 pool → 5 × $20,000 draw):

After the draw, burn/reset all Big Block Tickets to 0.

Small blocks stay super fair and fresh (no one carries old tickets forward).
Big blocks naturally accumulate (people can see their big block entries climbing over weeks/months).

\- Requires Stripe account verification

\- Credit card payments
\- OAuth authentication
\- Fiat → crypto conversion

Pros:
\- Uses the Coinbase brand trust

Cons:
\- Requires a Coinbase account
\- User needs to buy crypto first

I see one issue. Coinbase Commerce is NOT a true fiat/credit card payment processor - it's a cryptocurrency payment gateway. Users still need crypto to pay!

Let me explain what's happening and provide real solutions:
Coinbase Commerce requires users to:
1\. Have cryptocurrency (USDC, ETH, BTC, etc.)
2\. Send it from their wallet to complete payment
3\. It's NOT accepting credit cards directly
This means it's not suitable for true non-crypto users who don't have any cryptocurrency.

Real Fiat On-Ramp Solutions
For TRUE credit card payments (Visa/Mastercard), you need different services:

Option 1: Stripe + Crypto (Recommended)
Best for: Direct card payments + automatic blockchain transactions
Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Users never need crypto
\- Lower fees than crypto payments
\- Familiar checkout experience

Cons:
\- Requires Stripe account verification
\- 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Option 2: Coinbase Pay (Different from Commerce)
Coinbase Pay (not Commerce) supports:
\- Credit card payments
\- OAuth authentication
\- Fiat → crypto conversion

Pros:
\- Uses the Coinbase brand trust
\- Integrated fiat → crypto

Cons:
\- Requires a Coinbase account
\- User needs to buy crypto first

Option 3: Third-Party Fiat Gateways
Services that do true fiat → crypto:
\- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget
\- Ramp Network - Fiat on-ramp widget
\- Wyre - Fiat gateway (being sunset)
\- Transak - Global fiat on-ramp

Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Pre-built widgets
\- Global coverage

Cons:
\- Higher fees (3-5%)
\- KYC requirements
\- User still sees crypto conversion

I see one issue. Coinbase Commerce is NOT a true fiat/credit card payment processor - it's a cryptocurrency payment gateway. Users still need crypto to pay!

Let me explain what's happening and provide real solutions:
Coinbase Commerce requires users to:
1\. Have cryptocurrency (USDC, ETH, BTC, etc.)
2\. Send it from their wallet to complete payment
3\. It's NOT accepting credit cards directly
This means it's not suitable for true non-crypto users who don't have any cryptocurrency.

Real Fiat On-Ramp Solutions
For TRUE credit card payments (Visa/Mastercard), you need different services:

Option 1: Stripe + Crypto (Recommended)
Best for: Direct card payments + automatic blockchain transactions
Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Users never need crypto
\- Lower fees than crypto payments
\- Familiar checkout experience

Cons:
\- Requires Stripe account verification
\- 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Option 2: Coinbase Pay (Different from Commerce)
Coinbase Pay (not Commerce) supports:
\- Credit card payments
\- OAuth authentication
\- Fiat → crypto conversion

Pros:
\- Uses the Coinbase brand trust
\- Integrated fiat → crypto

Cons:
\- Requires a Coinbase account
\- User needs to buy crypto first

Option 3: Third-Party Fiat Gateways
Services that do true fiat → crypto:
\- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget
\- Ramp Network - Fiat on-ramp widget
\- Wyre - Fiat gateway (being sunset)
\- Transak - Global fiat on-ramp

Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Pre-built widgets
\- Global coverage

Cons:
\- Higher fees (3-5%)
\- KYC requirements
\- User still sees crypto conversion

\- Wraps all msg.value into WETH
\- Swaps all WETH to USDC
\- If usdcReceived > 15 USDC, it refunds the difference in USDC

To refund ETH instead, the contract must not swap the full amount.

history.speaker: freelancer

Best-practice approach (clean + safe UX)
Update mintWithETH to use Uniswap V3 exactOutputSingle:
\- Target exactly 15\_000\_000 USDC out
\- Provide amountInMaximum = msg.value WETH
\- Router uses only what’s needed
\- Contract unwraps leftover WETH and refunds ETH to the payer
\- Reverts if it can’t get 15 USDC within msg.value
\- This is the standard way to guarantee the exact USDC mint price and refund the remainder in ETH.

Recommendation
\- If you want zero surprises for users: implement exactOutputSingle + ETH refund (requires a redeploy).
\- If you want to keep things stable now: keep current behavior but add a short UI note like: “Excess is refunded in USDC.” (lowest risk).

I see one issue. Coinbase Commerce is NOT a true fiat/credit card payment processor - it's a cryptocurrency payment gateway. Users still need crypto to pay!

Let me explain what's happening and provide real solutions:
Coinbase Commerce requires users to:
1\. Have cryptocurrency (USDC, ETH, BTC, etc.)
2\. Send it from their wallet to complete payment
3\. It's NOT accepting credit cards directly
This means it's not suitable for true non-crypto users who don't have any cryptocurrency.

Real Fiat On-Ramp Solutions
For TRUE credit card payments (Visa/Mastercard), you need different services:

Option 1: Stripe + Crypto (Recommended)
Best for: Direct card payments + automatic blockchain transactions
Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Users never need crypto
\- Lower fees than crypto payments
\- Familiar checkout experience

Cons:
\- Requires Stripe account verification
\- 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Option 2: Coinbase Pay (Different from Commerce)
Coinbase Pay (not Commerce) supports:
\- Credit card payments
\- OAuth authentication
\- Fiat → crypto conversion

Pros:
\- Uses the Coinbase brand trust
\- Integrated fiat → crypto

Cons:
\- Requires a Coinbase account
\- User needs to buy crypto first

Option 3: Third-Party Fiat Gateways
Services that do true fiat → crypto:
\- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget
\- Ramp Network - Fiat on-ramp widget
\- Wyre - Fiat gateway (being sunset)
\- Transak - Global fiat on-ramp

Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Pre-built widgets
\- Global coverage

Cons:
\- Higher fees (3-5%)
\- KYC requirements
\- User still sees crypto conversion

Yes — it’s doable, and it’s not “crazy complicated”, but it does require changing the on-chain flow (i.e., a contract update / redeploy of the NFT contract’s mintWithETH logic). With the current design (swap full msg.value → USDC, then refund excess in USDC), the contract simply doesn’t have a path to refund ETH.

Why it requires a contract change
Right now mintWithETH:
\- Wraps all msg.value into WETH
\- Swaps all WETH to USDC
\- If usdcReceived > 15 USDC, it refunds the difference in USDC

To refund ETH instead, the contract must not swap the full amount.

history.speaker: freelancer
history.text:
Best-practice approach (clean + safe UX)
Update mintWithETH to use Uniswap V3 exactOutputSingle:
\- Target exactly 15\_000\_000 USDC out
\- Provide amountInMaximum = msg.value WETH
\- Router uses only what’s needed
\- Contract unwraps leftover WETH and refunds ETH to the payer
\- Reverts if it can’t get 15 USDC within msg.value
\- This is the standard way to guarantee the exact USDC mint price and refund the remainder in ETH.

Recommendation
\- If you want zero surprises for users: implement exactOutputSingle + ETH refund (requires a redeploy).
\- If you want to keep things stable now: keep current behavior but add a short UI note like: “Excess is refunded in USDC.” (lowest risk).

Hey Joseph,
One final-final mechanics tweak that actually makes everything cleaner and simpler to code (no weird half-expiring tickets).
New rule (replaces the previous ticket lifespan description):
→ Every time someone mints with a referral code, the referrer instantly gets two separate tickets added to their NFT:
+1 Small Block Ticket
+1 Big Block Ticket

These are two completely independent counters.
Small Block ($2,500 pool → 5 × $500 draw):
Draw only from Small Block Tickets issued since the last small block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Small Block Tickets to 0.
Big Block ($100,000 pool → 5 × $20,000 draw):
Draw only from Big Block Tickets issued since the last big block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Big Block Tickets to 0.

This way:
Small blocks stay super fair and fresh (no one carries old tickets forward).
Big blocks naturally accumulate (people can see their big block entries climbing over weeks/months).
Metadata is trivial: just show the two counters + permanent badges.

Triggers stay pool-based (small block fires the moment small pool = exactly $2,500, big block when big pool = exactly $100,000). Secondary royalties still fill pools but don’t create tickets.
Everything else stays identical (auto $5 commission, random ticket to existing NFT when no ref used, manual claim, etc.).
This version should be easier to implement and explain to users.
Sorry for the flip-flop — Once you confirm this is cleaner for you too, we’re 100% locked.

I see one issue. Coinbase Commerce is NOT a true fiat/credit card payment processor - it's a cryptocurrency payment gateway. Users still need crypto to pay!

Let me explain what's happening and provide real solutions:
Coinbase Commerce requires users to:
1\. Have cryptocurrency (USDC, ETH, BTC, etc.)
2\. Send it from their wallet to complete payment
3\. It's NOT accepting credit cards directly
This means it's not suitable for true non-crypto users who don't have any cryptocurrency.

Real Fiat On-Ramp Solutions
For TRUE credit card payments (Visa/Mastercard), you need different services:

Option 1: Stripe + Crypto (Recommended)
Best for: Direct card payments + automatic blockchain transactions
Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Users never need crypto
\- Lower fees than crypto payments
\- Familiar checkout experience

Cons:
\- Requires Stripe account verification
\- 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Option 2: Coinbase Pay (Different from Commerce)
Coinbase Pay (not Commerce) supports:
\- Credit card payments
\- OAuth authentication
\- Fiat → crypto conversion

Pros:
\- Uses the Coinbase brand trust
\- Integrated fiat → crypto

Cons:
\- Requires a Coinbase account
\- User needs to buy crypto first

Option 3: Third-Party Fiat Gateways
Services that do true fiat → crypto:
\- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget
\- Ramp Network - Fiat on-ramp widget
\- Wyre - Fiat gateway (being sunset)
\- Transak - Global fiat on-ramp

Pros:
\- Real credit card payments
\- Pre-built widgets
\- Global coverage

Cons:
\- Higher fees (3-5%)
\- KYC requirements
\- User still sees crypto conversion

Yes — it’s doable, and it’s not “crazy complicated”, but it does require changing the on-chain flow (i.e., a contract update / redeploy of the NFT contract’s mintWithETH logic). With the current design (swap full msg.value → USDC, then refund excess in USDC), the contract simply doesn’t have a path to refund ETH.

Why it requires a contract change
Right now mintWithETH:
\- Wraps all msg.value into WETH
\- Swaps all WETH to USDC
\- If usdcReceived > 15 USDC, it refunds the difference in USDC

To refund ETH instead, the contract must not swap the full amount.

history.speaker: freelancer
history.text:
Best-practice approach (clean + safe UX)
Update mintWithETH to use Uniswap V3 exactOutputSingle:
\- Target exactly 15\_000\_000 USDC out
\- Provide amountInMaximum = msg.value WETH
\- Router uses only what’s needed
\- Contract unwraps leftover WETH and refunds ETH to the payer
\- Reverts if it can’t get 15 USDC within msg.value
\- This is the standard way to guarantee the exact USDC mint price and refund the remainder in ETH.

Recommendation
\- If you want zero surprises for users: implement exactOutputSingle + ETH refund (requires a redeploy).
\- If you want to keep things stable now: keep current behavior but add a short UI note like: “Excess is refunded in USDC.” (lowest risk).

Hey Joseph,
One final-final mechanics tweak that actually makes everything cleaner and simpler to code (no weird half-expiring tickets).
New rule (replaces the previous ticket lifespan description):
→ Every time someone mints with a referral code, the referrer instantly gets two separate tickets added to their NFT:
+1 Small Block Ticket
+1 Big Block Ticket

These are two completely independent counters.
Small Block ($2,500 pool → 5 × $500 draw):
Draw only from Small Block Tickets issued since the last small block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Small Block Tickets to 0.
Big Block ($100,000 pool → 5 × $20,000 draw):
Draw only from Big Block Tickets issued since the last big block.
After the draw, burn/reset all Big Block Tickets to 0.

This way:
Small blocks stay super fair and fresh (no one carries old tickets forward).
Big blocks naturally accumulate (people can see their big block entries climbing over weeks/months).
Metadata is trivial: just show the two counters + permanent badges.

Triggers stay pool-based (small block fires the moment small pool = exactly $2,500, big block when big pool = exactly $100,000). Secondary royalties still fill pools but don’t create tickets.
Everything else stays identical (auto $5 commission, random ticket to existing NFT when no ref used, manual claim, etc.).
This version should be easier to implement and explain to users.
Sorry for the flip-flop — Once you confirm this is cleaner for you too, we’re 100% locked.

Thanks man!
